tasks.short: Attend meetings, conferences and training workshops.

steps.what: Read the posted session line for this workshop.
Attend the meeting, conference or teacher training workshop.

tasks.design: The kindergarten teacher still attends the meeting, conference or teacher training workshop. A session line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with session title, date, place, focus and the author's name, so the hunt for that sheet is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The session line sat on a paper sheet, so the teacher hunted it before attending the workshop.
tasks.enabler_now: The staff file already holds a session line. Showing session title, date, place, focus and the author's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: What the teacher takes from the workshop is what happens in the room. A posted line does not attend.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher hears the session and refuses a line that does not name this workshop.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the classroom and the workshop. Less time goes to hunting a session sheet. The teacher still attends.

reach.task: Post the session line before the workshop.
reach.learn: The line needs session title, date, place, focus and the author's name, or the teacher reads the paper sheet.

reach.task: Leave the workshop attendance with this teacher.
reach.learn: Attending a workshop is the teacher's own work. It is not a send.

reach.task: Stay with the class while the teacher attends.
reach.learn: The assistant does not attend in the teacher's place, and does not file the hours.

evidence.claim: Attending the conference or the teacher training workshop stays with the kindergarten teacher. A posted session line can be a shorter read. The attendance itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
AI that admits pupils, evaluates learning outcomes, sets the education level or watches tests is high-risk. This design does none of those. The teacher attends in person.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned. This design does not infer emotions and does not watch the workshop with a model.
Works-council law does not apply to schools. Staff must consent before a tool can monitor them. This design does not record the workshop and does not monitor the teacher.
The posted line is a session title, date, place and focus. It is not a pupil record. National school rules vary. The digest names the Netherlands for the school participation law.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only attending the professional meeting, educational conference or teacher training workshop. Teaching the class, staff committees, classroom stock and hall duty sit outside it. The instructional coordinator posts the line before the session.

Structured input: one session line in the {DOCS} with session title, date, place, focus and the author's name. The line is the session topic, not a pupil record and not a training-hours record. If the line is missing or free text, the teacher reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The teacher still attends in the room. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit and no send, so there is no gate on a sent version. The prior that attending is a send outside the organisation is refused: it is the teacher's own presence, and it is a write inside the organisation. The design does not register the teacher and does not file the hours.
A model is not used. Existing system runtime is not the teacher's time. The design does not evaluate a pupil, infer emotions, record the workshop, monitor the teacher, or file a note.
unknowns: Whether this staff file already has session title, date, place, focus and a name, or only a paper sheet.
Whether the school later wants the hours filed. This design does not file them.
research_questions: Who posts the session line, the instructional coordinator or the school office?
What share of workshops start with no line the teacher can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text session sheet by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the session line still names this workshop, date, place, focus and an author.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the session line is often missing or free text, so the teacher still hunts the paper sheet and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry session title, date, place, focus and an author's name, and only that hunt shrinks. Attending stays. The high stays under the net after the field check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select, store, issue and inventory classroom supplies.

steps.what: Read the posted stock line for this classroom.
Select, store, issue and inventory classroom equipment, materials and supplies.

tasks.design: The kindergarten teacher still selects, stores, issues and inventories the classroom equipment, materials and supplies. A stock line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with item, place, quantity on hand, date and the author's name, so the hunt for that sheet is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The stock line sat on a paper sheet, so the teacher hunted it before counting the cupboard.
tasks.enabler_now: The classroom file already holds a stock line. Showing item, place, quantity on hand, date and the author's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: What the class needs, and what is actually on the shelf, is what the teacher sees in the room. A posted line does not count.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the cupboard and refuses a line that does not name this classroom.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the cupboard and the classroom. Less time goes to hunting a stock sheet. The teacher still selects and counts.

reach.task: Post the stock line before the count.
reach.learn: The line needs item, place, quantity on hand, date and the author's name, or the teacher reads the paper sheet.

reach.task: Set materials out only when the teacher asks.
reach.learn: The teacher still selects, stores, issues and counts. The assistant does not send an order.

reach.task: Leave this classroom's cupboard with this teacher.
reach.learn: Counting this room is a write inside the organisation. It is not a send.

evidence.claim: Selecting, storing, issuing and counting classroom equipment, materials and supplies stay with the kindergarten teacher. A posted stock line can be a shorter read. The count itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.
AI that admits pupils, evaluates learning outcomes, sets the education level or watches tests is high-risk. This design does none of those. The teacher counts in the room.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned. This design does not infer emotions and does not watch the cupboard with a model.
Works-council law does not apply to schools. Staff must consent before a tool can monitor them. This design does not record the count and does not monitor the teacher.

The posted line is an item, a place, a quantity on hand, a date and a name. It is not a pupil record and not an order. National school rules vary. The digest names the Netherlands for the school participation law.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only selecting, storing, issuing and counting classroom equipment, materials and supplies in this room. Workshops, committees and hall duty sit outside it. The instructional coordinator posts the line before the count.

Structured input: one stock line in the {DOCS} with item, place, quantity on hand, date and the author's name. The line is what was last written down, not the live count and not a pupil record. If the line is missing or free text, the teacher reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The teacher still selects, stores, issues and counts in the room. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit and no send, so there is no gate on a sent version. A supplier order would be its own step, with a gate on the final version. That step is not in this design, and it is not folded into the count. Counting is a write inside the organisation. The prior that this task sends outside the organisation is refused.

A model is not used. Existing system runtime is not the teacher's time. The design does not evaluate a pupil, infer emotions, record the count, monitor the teacher, file a stock note, or send an order.
unknowns: Whether this classroom file already has item, place, quantity on hand, date and a name, or only a paper sheet.
Whether the school later wants a supplier order. This design does not send one.
